r6458s:262: The article highlights a technical detail that is easy to overlook: the regulatory domain is full of acronyms (e.g., AML, KYC, GDPR), and users often use these acronyms when asking questions. Amazon adopted a Query Expansion strategy—using Claude 3.5 Haiku to generate up to 5 query variants and calling the retrieval API in parallel. This not only solves the acronym problem but also improves recall through multi-path retrieval. The key engineering optimization lies in parallel processing: latency dropped from 10 seconds under sequential processing to below 2 seconds under parallel processing. This optimization reveals an important engineering intuition—in RAG systems, retrieval latency is often the user experience bottleneck, and parallelization is the most direct way to reduce latency.
